data.title: Worldcoin price prediction — What next after $4.7M long liquidation flush fuels 13% fall?
data.description:
Worldcoin [WLD] recorded another bout of intense selling. CoinMarketCap data showed the daily trading volume for the altcoin rose by 33.6%, even though we are heading into a weekend, which generally sees reduced volume.

Alongside the sizeable volume hike, the price fell by 13.55% in 24 hours. Meanwhile, Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] shed 1.26% and 1.47% of their values in the same window, respectively.

Worldcoin-specific selling also triggered $4.68 million in long liquidations on Friday, 23rd October. The short liquidations on the day were only $517.8K by comparison.

Examining WLD’s price structure

On the 1-hour chart, a bullish structure was established in early September when the altcoin rallied past the swing level at $0.45 and closed a daily session above it. After retracing to a swing low of $0.356, the altcoin rallied to new highs at $0.619, keeping the bullish structure intact.

Worldcoin remained inside this bullish structure, despite the drawdown in recent days and the range formation of recent weeks.

The CMF was at +0.0, exactly neutral, highlighting the bulls’ and bears’ even influence on capital flows. The MACD was slowly falling towards neutral zero, while the RSI slipped below neutral-50 to signal a bearish momentum shift on this timeframe.

Worldcoin fails to sustain range breakout

In a recent report, AMBCrypto highlighted the short-term range formation between $0.46 and $0.58. On Wednesday, 21st October, the price closed a 4-hour session above $0.58, but this breakout didn’t last long.

Less than three days later, WLD had seen a 21.3% retracement, from $0.598 to $0.471 at the time of writing. The technical indicators unanimously showed sizeable capital outflows and downward momentum on the 4-hour chart.

Since the daily structure was bullish, not all hope may be lost though. The $0.48-range lows might be defended. Even if the short-term range is lost, swing traders can keep an eye on the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $0.412 for a buying opportunity.

Final Summary

  • Worldcoin’s price trajectory took a swift 180-degree turn earlier in the week, and shed nearly 22% in just over three days.
  • Bulls still have a chance to turn the momentum around at the range lows or the $0.412 retracement level.

data.title: ‘Unacceptable’ — Kraken apologizes, scraps Monero withdrawal questions
data.description:
Kraken exchange co-CEO Arjun Sethi has apologized for emails sent to Monero [XMR] buyers.

The infamous emails contained questionnaires asking XMR buyers to state their employers, proof of income, bank statements, and what they plan to do with the withdrawn funds. 

Part of the email sent by Kraken Support, and widely shared across social networks, including Reddit, read,

We noticed Monero [XMR] withdrawals from your Kraken account. Could you explain the rationale and purpose of these transactions, including the intended use of XMR following withdrawals

Many in the community warned that Kraken is taking the Monero crackdown to “another level,” with some cautioning other users to expect similar questions. 

Following widespread community backlash, Kraken co-CEO responded to the same. He noted that the emails have been withdrawn. 

Kraken’s Sethi: Monero’s XMR stays listed

In an X post, Arjun Sethi clarified that the exchange’s reaction was not based on any required rule, but a false red flag. 

The $XMR emails were ours. They were wrong, unacceptable. No rule required it. Someone saw a young client with a lot of money and called it a red flag. That is not a red flag. That is our customer and client.

He added, 

Where your money came from is a fair question. What you do with it after it leaves is not. XMR stays listed. Buy it here, take it home.

Most of Kraken’s operations in the EU, UK, and Canada have banned XMR trading. This is partly due to compliance. In fact, the EU plans to ban crypto custody of privacy coins from mid-2027. 

Still, individual ownership is not outright illegal via self-custody wallets. What’s banned is trading them across regulated venues. 

Kraken U.S is the last platform yet to ban XMR. However, since August, it has placed individual and corporate monthly caps on the privacy coin. Individuals can deposit a maximum of $3,500 worth of XMR and only withdraw up to $1,500 per month. For firms, the limits are $30K and $10K, respectively. 

Impact on XMR’s price

The infamous emails triggered a wave of selling pressure as XMR exchange inflows spiked over the past two days across Kraken and Bitfinex platforms. 

It dragged XMR’s price from the recent high of $659.6 to a low of $564, marking a 14% price pullback. Still, the decline could stop if buyers defend the support zone above $520, in alignment with the exponential moving averages (EMA). 

Final Summary

  • Kraken’s co-CEO Sethi said they scrapped the XMR withdrawals, calling it ‘wrong’ and ‘unacceptable.’
  • XMR slumped by 14% amid the FUD, but whether Sethi’s statement will renew demand remains unclear.

data.title: Ethereum outflows hit 4-month high – Why ETH price still risks $2,300
data.description:
Ethereum [ETH] registered its largest daily exchange outflows in over four months, with 169,770 ETH leaving exchanges as market participants anticipate a potential price rebound. Santiment Intelligence is comparing the recent withdrawals to a similar spike recorded on the 5th of June.

Following that period, Ethereum recorded roughly 223,800 ETH in net outflows as its price reached a local bottom. Subsequently, the token staged a strong price rebound, making the later withdrawal spike particularly significant to the prevailing market conditions.

For context, substantial exchange withdrawals generally limit the amount of ETH readily available for immediate selling. Therefore, this recent development reinforced expectations of a possible price recovery, even though historical patterns sometimes offer no guarantee.

Meanwhile, selling activity among Ethereum’s earliest investors introduced another important  factor into the recovery story.

Ethereum OG whales cash out after years

According to Lookonchain, an early Ethereum investor reportedly sold 3,000 ETH valued approximately $7.23 million. Originally, the investor purchased the tokens nine years ago at just $18.83 each, which secured a reported 128-fold return.

Beside that, another Ethereum OG separately sold 1,000 ETH after acquiring tokens during Ethereum’s initial coin offering. This investor originally purchased 100,000 ETH at around $0.31 per token. The two long-term holders together sold 4,000 ETH, which highlighted renewed selling activity among Ethereum’s earliest investors.

Even though the reported exchange withdrawals implied limited available supply, the whale transactions showed continued selling among long-term investors.

Also notably, Ethereum’s derivatives market also highlighted persistent selling pressure, beyond these individual sales.

Futures sellers maintain control over ETH

As per CryptoQuant analytics, Ethereum’s Futures Taker CVD continued showing seller dominance, which implied sustained aggressive selling activity. In particular, this indicator measured the cumulative divergence between market buy and sell orders across the Futures markets of ETH.

The seller-dominant reading therefore  indicated that aggressive sellers continued outweighing buyers throughout the period observed. This derivatives positioning was in contrast with the considerable exchange withdrawals reported by Santiment.

Consequently, such positioning could likely invalidate recovery prospects, especially in case the aggressive Futures selling persists alongside the prevailing weak ETH price action.

Can Ethereum defend $2,300?

The daily timeframe chart highlighted continued weakness after ETH failed to sustain its earlier recovery toward the $2,540.68 price level. The altcoin subsequently pulled back toward $2,376.62, losing its key support at the $2,385.62 price level.

Notably, the latest candles highlighted repeated attempts to stabilize around this zone, but the bulls did not manage to establish a convincing rebound.

Meanwhile, the Parabolic SAR indicator remained above the prevailing market value at $2,509.93 as of writing, strengthening the current bearish structure.

Furthermore, the MACD indicator maintained a bearish crossover. Notably, the indicator’s negative histogram reading of -8.90 further validated that the bears retained the technical advantage.

Overall, the bearish technical indicators for now outweighed the bullish implications of exchange withdrawals. Unless the bulls reclaim the $2,385 support, ETH could face further price decline toward $2,300.

Final Thoughts

  • Ethereum’s exchange outflows reached a four-month high, but early investors continued selling their holdings. 
  • Persistent Futures selling and bearish indicators left ETH facing another potential decline toward $2,300.

data.title: GRAM crypto crashes 11% as long liquidations hit $5.8M – What’s next?
data.description:
Gram [GRAM], formerly Toncoin, fell 5.77% in the past 24 hours. On the 23rd of October, the altcoin’s price fell 11.08% in just one hour, from $1.30 to $1.15. Incidentally, this price dip was the first time GRAM fell below the $1.30 demand zone that has been kept intact since early August.

The price drop caused a cascade of long liquidations. CoinGlass liquidation data revealed that $5.83 million in long liquidations across all exchanges was recorded on Friday, compared to just $240.3k in short liquidations.

Buyer exhaustion at a key support zone combined with a liquidation cascade helped explain the recent GRAM losses.

How traders can capitalize on GRAM’s bearish bias

Toward the end of September, the altcoin rallied to a high of $1.74. Since it had also breached the $1.56 high made in August, it appeared to confirm a bullish price trend.

Strong derivatives and spot volumes back then, combined with bullish expectations for Bitcoin [BTC] as it rallied back above $80k, reinforced the positive GRAM outlook.

Since then, the market-wide buyer apathy led to a steep pullback for the altcoin. It dropped into the $1.30-$1.35 demand zone, highlighted in cyan. This region has been defended for nearly three months, but failed in the past 24 hours.

The A/D indicator highlighted a lack of buying pressure in recent days. The H4 MACD made a bearish crossover earlier in the week, drawing attention to the rising bearish momentum.

Moreover, swing traders should remain bearish because the price has decisively broken below both a key support zone and the previous swing low.

GRAM traders’ call to action: Sell the bounce!

The $1.30-$1.35 former demand zone is now a supply zone. GRAM could be oversold in the short-term and has the potential to bounce to this supply zone before another bearish impulse move.

Traders can wait for such a retest, and the next bearish crossover on the MACD, to look to go short. Meanwhile, a sustained recovery back above $1.36 would indicate a bounce that could reach $1.50-$1.60 before running out of steam.

Final Summary

  • GRAM, formerly Toncoin, saw an intense wave of selling that led to an 11% price drop within an hour of trading on Friday.
  • Heavy spot selling volume and a cascade of long liquidations helped fuel the swift price drop to $1.15, shifting swing traders’ bias bearishly.

data.title: Bitcoin ETF outflows hit $635M as BTC price tests $81K support
data.description:
Spot Bitcoin [BTC] ETF recorded its biggest outflows since June 2025 on the 22nd of October, 2026, worth $635.5 million.

On the same day, BlackRock’s IBIT led the withdrawals with $254.1 million. This was followed by Fidelity’s FBTC at $217.5 million, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB at $109.4 million, Bitwise’s BITB at $27.4 million, and Grayscale’s GBTC at $29.5 million.

In fact, together, these products accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow. Meanwhile, on the other hand, Morgan Stanley’s MSBT recorded a relatively small $2.3 million inflow that provided little offset to the broader selling pressure.

Trend reversal

The scale of the withdrawals was particularly striking because it erased the positive momentum built up during the preceding two sessions, which had collectively attracted more than $1.05 billion.

In fact, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin ETFs recorded a massive $663 million in inflows, marking their largest single-day intake in two months.

At the same time, Switzerland’s FINMA approved a physically backed Bitcoin fund, BBIT, for retail investors, with trading expected to begin on the SIX Swiss Exchange in November.

Bitcoin is back near the $81K radar

This BTC ETF rollercoaster came as Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours but a drop of over 5% in the past month.

In other words, Bitcoin is once again back in the playground, where it is testing the $81,000 level. That said, Glassnode describes this price level as the estimated cost basis of investors in U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs.

For those unaware, the ETF cost basis refers to the average price at which investors acquired Bitcoin exposure through these funds. This level usually influences investor behavior.

So, if BTC remains above $81,000, the level could act as support and help stabilize the market. However, a sustained break below the $81K price level could weaken sentiment, particularly among investors who entered the market around this price.

Did altcoin ETFs mirror BTC ETFs?

On the other hand, other altcoin ETFs somewhat followed a similar pattern as BTC ETFs.

According to SoSo Value data, Ethereum [ETH] ETFs recorded $110.50 million in outflows, followed by Solana [SOL] ETF, which saw $8.51 million in outflows, and Hyperliquid [HYPE] ETF, which saw $7.88 million worth of outflows.

Notably, the newly launched Zcash [ZEC] ETF recorded $14.23 million in inflows, followed by the XRP ETF, which saw inflows worth $3.55 million all this on the 22nd of October.

Final Summary

  • BlackRock’s IBIT, Fidelity’s FBTC, ARK 21Shares’ ARKB, Bitwise’s BITB, and Grayscale’s GBTC accounted for the bulk of the daily outflow.
  • Bitcoin was trading at $81,612.79 at press time after a modest drop in the past 24 hours.

data.title: Initia halts L1 and rollups after $2.7 million exploit — What happened?
data.description:
Initia, a Layer 1 blockchain and interwoven modular roll-up network, suffered a major security incident on 23rd October. An attacker allegedly exploited a vulnerability in its blockchain to create tokens without permission and withdraw real assets from cross-chain bridges. 

According to the investigation, the attack began at 14:59:26 UTC when the exploiter used a single signed transaction to mint 2 million AUSD tokens out of thin air on Initia.

The transaction reportedly consumed 135,888 gas and called a ‘Move’ function directly, without requiring a cross-chain bridge message. So, instead of breaking the bridge’s security verification process directly, the attacker hacked a vulnerability in the token-minting mechanism.

All about Initia’s security incident

The attacker didn’t stop there though. Instead, they exploited cross-chain infrastructure to convert these unauthorized tokens into real assets on Ethereum [ETH]. So, roughly 153 seconds after the initial mint, a valid LayerZero message enabled the release of 1.4 million AUSD from the Ethereum-side adapter.

At the same time, the attacker also withdrew 105 ETH from the native-ETH adapter and obtained 1.08 million USDC through Circle’s Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP). According to researchers, the attacker converted the funds into Ethereum through decentralized trading services, including 1inch and 0x.

Here, within approximately 7 minutes of the initial mint, around $2.65 million had reached Ethereum. The consolidated funds later amounted to 1,135.52 ETH, worth approximately $2.73 million, held in a newly created wallet.

This seemed to be very similar to September’s Liquid Network incident, where a software bug enabled the creation of unauthorized L-BTC and the withdrawal of real Bitcoin.

As expected, the incident forced Initia to halt its L1 blockchain and roll-ups. And yet, despite this rollercoaster, Initia’s token INIT was trading at $0.1484 at press time after a hike of 11.7% in the last 24 hours. 

2026 has so far being a tricky year for security incidents like these. In fact, AMBCrypto’s recent report found that crypto security losses surged by 55% to $1.18 billion in Q3 2026, while reported incidents jumped from 67 to 107. 

Final Summary

  • Transaction reportedly consumed 135,888 gas and called a ‘Move’ function directly, without requiring a cross-chain bridge message.
  • This was very similar to September’s Liquid Network incident, where a software bug enabled the creation of unauthorized L-BTC and the withdrawal of real Bitcoin.

data.title: Ethereum’s deflationary edge fades – Is an ETH/BTC breakout still possible?
data.description:
Ethereum’s [ETH] deflationary edge over Bitcoin may be fading.

Since the merge, 55.4% of the newly issued ETH has been burned. However, this number has dropped significantly to only 2.7% over the last thirty days. In addition, ETH’s yearly supply growth has increased to 0.86%, which is almost Bitcoin’s 0.82%. That’s a sharp pullback in ETH burning, impacting its scarcity argument and potentially challenging the long-term bullish thesis versus BTC.

So, with ETH’s deflationary narrative being challenged, its next leg higher could increasingly rely on demand for Ethereum’s Layer 1 block space. As the chart below shows, gas prices have dropped from 2.76 Gwei to just 0.03 Gwei in two days, fueling the “Is ETH the new SOL?” debate. But cheaper prices are not always good, as they can also signal weaker demand for the block space.

Notably, this is where a key on-chain metric comes into play. 

According to CryptoQuant data, Ethereum Velocity is at 11.03, implying that ETH is circulated actively on the blockchain. Moreover, the number of active addresses has hit 627k, suggesting growing adoption. And if the demand is sustained on a declining gas fee, the cost to transact on ETH will remain cheap despite active use.

In this context, declining gas fees could be a bullish sign, which brings ETH/BTC back to the forefront. While Ethereum’s deflationary edge is being eroded, strong Layer 1 activity could offset it. The important question is whether ongoing on-chain demand will catalyze a rebound in ETH/BTC. In turn, translate into a stronger relative performance against Bitcoin [BTC].

Ethereum’s bullish positioning raises hopes of BTC outperformance

The divergence between ETH’s technical and fundamental setup is growing interesting.

While the overall whale activity seems to be cooling, the Bitfinex whales’ ETH long positions are rising sharply, suggesting smart money is positioning for further upside. Meanwhile, ETH/BTC is also showing a pattern similar to its pre-altseason setup in 2021, forming higher highs and retesting its trendline.

On-chain data adds another bullish sign. According to Santiment, about 169k ETH left exchanges on a net basis. This marked the largest daily outflow in more than four months. A similar development occurred on the 5th of June when roughly 223,800 ETH left exchanges as ETH reached its lowest price since the beginning of April 2025, only to climb rapidly in the following days.

Taken together, strong network activity, rising whale longs, and a significant ETH exchange outflow make up Ethereum’s bullish case. Should ETH/BTC follow the same pattern as it did in 2021 ahead of the altseason, another breakout could be on the way.

The logic is simple: While Ethereum’s advantage over Bitcoin in terms of deflationary properties has weakened, an increase in layer 1 demand, rising whale longs, and ongoing exchange outflows may create conditions for a supply squeeze. Taken together, these factors suggest ETH could be building momentum for a potential breakout against BTC once the market turns back to risk-on.

data.title: Here’s why XRP’s price recovery faces threat from surge in whale inflows
data.description:
The Spot ETF flows to XRP in October have totaled +$14.52 million so far. The ETF inflows were not enough to halt the 13.4% price decline in October though, with the altcoin falling from $1.49 to $1.29 at the time of writing.

In mid-September, XRP tested the $1.25 local demand zone and saw a bullish price reaction that boosted the token up to $1.65. The retracement since then, including the steady losses in October, has driven the price back to the same demand zone.

XRP bulls look to hold on to $1.25 for a second time

AMBCrypto recently reported that the share of exchange transactions amounting to more than one million XRP dropped from 60% to 38.6%. It highlighted a slowdown in large-holder transfers, and their lower accumulation interest could help explain XRP’s price decline.

While the swing structure on the 1-day chart remained bullish, XRP settled into a range formation in recent months. The $1.27-$1.31 demand zone is the one swing traders will want to watch, anticipating a bullish price reaction.

Increased whale inflows threaten recovery potential

Crypto intelligence platform Santiment observed that the number of non-empty wallets on the XRP Ledger has been rising steadily, despite the price volatility in recent months.

Moreover, the number of new XRP wallets created in a day jumped to 4,772, the fifth-biggest spike this metric has seen since March. Fresh participation and holder growth could boost demand too.

At the same time, XRP inflows from whales (defined as exceeding 1 million tokens) to Binance have accelerated in recent weeks. The monthly inflow average has increased from $72 million in August to $112.4 million. These figures are the highest since March, according to crypto analyst Darkfost.

In fact, they were above the $90 million monthly average recorded in the past three months, and there have been daily spikes of $400 million, reinforcing the claim that whale selling has intensified.

Right now, whale inflows have retraced to typical levels, but a trend in the opposite direction would be more encouraging for investors and swing traders looking to buy at the $1.25 demand zone.

Final Summary

  • On-chain activity with holder growth and new wallets created on the XRP Ledger reflected positively on the altcoin.
  • Steady selling pressure, including from whales, drove the drawdown from $1.65 to $1.29.

data.title: Starknet TVL crashes 3.7x to $42M after getting 93% vote to become L1
data.description:
Starknet got an overwhelming vote approval to become an independent layer 1 (L1) chain, but suffered a massive DeFi activity blow. The Ethereum L2 saw its total value locked (TVL) drop by 3.7x (73%) from $158M to $42M on 22nd October. 

The crash was triggered by Extended, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, which migrated from Starknet to Circle-backed Arc blockchain. The platform had a strategic partnership with Circle and sought higher performance. 

Extended migrated $120M in TVL, suggesting that it was the sole driver of Starknet’s DeFi activity. 

Similarly, Starknet’s stablecoin liquidity dropped by 75% from $147M to $37M over the same period. The bridged volumes also crashed, underscoring the dominance the Extended had in the L2. 

Will Starknet hold up after 93% support for L1 migration?

That said, Starknet plans to transition from an Ethereum L2 to an independent L1. The Starknet team, led by Eli Ben-Sasson, first floated the idea in early October.

Ben-Sasson argued that Ethereum’s post-quantum plan is too slow and may undermine the chain’s security plans amid increasing double threats from advanced AI models and quantum breakthroughs. 

A formal proposal for the same was put to a governance vote on 15th October. The proposal got massive 93% support, urging Starknet to research ways to become an L1. 

Following the vote, Sasson said StarkWare and the Starknet Foundation will allocate resources to begin the research. He added, 

STRK will remain the token of the network. Any path to transition to an L1 will be brought to a community vote. This is a huge shift and a milestone, but the AI and quantum challenges ahead require it.

Despite the overwhelming vote approval, however, STRK’s price chart was surprisingly negative. 

Starknet’s STRK reverses October gains

In early October, the L1 proposal sent STRK rallying by over +120% from $0.05 to $0.12. However, what followed was intense profit-taking, triggering a 58% loss and effectively reversing October’s gains. 

In fact, the pullback slipped below the EMA (exponential moving average) band. Simply put, STRK flipped bearish and shed another 7% on 22nd October. Unless the broader market sentiment improves, STRK could stay below the EMA bands for a while. 

Final Summary

  • Starknet TVL has crashed by 73% after Extended perps platform migrated $120M to Arc.
  • Team plans to begin L1 research pathways, but STRK reversed all of October’s gains.

data.title: Can DASH crypto rally further after a 77% surge in Futures volume?
data.description:
Dash [DASH], the privacy cryptocurrency, has been on the rise, with the asset crossing over 10% in gains in the early hours of the 23rd of  October. Notably, market sentiment points to further upside for DASH as bullish momentum continues to build.

DASH bullish momentum strengthens

Based on recent movements in the Aroon and Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicators, chart analysis suggests that DASH may continue to rise.

At the time of writing, the Aroon indicator showed that the Aroon Up (orange line) had crossed above the Aroon Down (blue line), suggesting there has been more buying pressure.

Often, the greater the disparity between the Aroon Up and the Aroon Down, the stronger the buying pressure in the market.

Therefore, the market remains bullish, with a reading of 100.00% for the Aroon Up and 42.86% for the Aroon Down, confirming that bulls are still in control.

Additionally, the bullish outlook has intensified with the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), which has formed a bullish crossover, with the blue MACD line crossing above the orange signal line.

This classic bullish formation often attracts more buyers as investors continue to accumulate the asset.

Funding Rate and OI rise

Capital positioning in the perpetual market has hinted at why there has been a surge in DASH’s performance.

The Funding Rate, an indicator that tracks capital positioning in the perpetual market and categorizes it as predominantly long or short, shows that the former is the case.

The Funding Rate moved from the negative territory of -0.0080% to a high of 0.0056% as writing. A positive Funding Rate indicates that long positions outweigh short positions in the perpetual market.

Likewise, there has been a surge in capital inflows into the perpetual market as the Funding Rate turned positive.

Open Interest (OI) surged by over 16%, with an additional $14 million in fresh capital inflows, putting DASH’s total perpetual market capital at roughly $87.62 million as of this writing.

The surge in the Funding Rate and OI also points to investors rotating capital into DASH’s perpetual market as they anticipate a further rally.

DASH sentiment and volume improve

Sentiment and volume remain largely positive, as the consensus among investors is that DASH is likely to sustain its surge in the near term.

At press time, sentiment for DASH stood at 4.22, implying a strong bullish outlook and suggesting that investors are likely to keep accumulating the asset.

CoinMarketCap’s sentiment scale ranges from -10 to 10. When sentiment is significantly positive, as it is for DASH, there is a greater likelihood of the rally continuing.

Likewise, there has been a noticeable surge in volume. In the perpetual market alone, trading volume was up 77%, reaching $218 million. Volume and price rising at the same time strengthen the case for an asset sustaining its upward move.

Final Summary

  • DASH gained over 10% as the Aroon and MACD formed a bullish crossover, suggesting further upside potential.
  • DASH’s Funding Rate turned positive at 0.0056%, while Open Interest rose over 16% and perpetual trading volume climbed 77% to $218 million, pointing to increased bullish positioning.
